title: Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K
summary: Given an integer array and a length k, find the highest sum of any k-length subarray where all elements are unique.
statement: Given an integer array and a length k, find the highest sum of any k-length subarray where all elements are unique. If no such subarray exists, return 0. A subarray is a continuous segment of the original array.
constraints: Consider every contiguous subarray of exactly length k.
A window qualifies only when all k values are distinct.
Return the largest qualifying sum, or zero when no window qualifies.
hints: Maintain a length-k sliding window with a running sum and frequency map.
Add the new value and remove the value that falls k positions behind.
A size-k window has all distinct values exactly when the map contains k keys.
Every length-k window is visited once, and the maximum updates only for precisely qualifying windows.
editorial: Every length-k window is visited once, and the maximum updates only for precisely qualifying windows.

tests.explanation: Distinct windows [1,5,4], [5,4,2], and [4,2,9] sum to 10, 11, and 15, so the answer is 15.
Every length-two window repeats 4, so none qualifies and the answer is zero.
